meta.source: 4th Autonomous Greenhouse Challenge: Dwarf Tomato Timeseries and Images (Maree et al., 4TU.ResearchData, CC BY 4.0), via the derived tables in out/dash/. Scoring rules: Maree et al. 2025, Sensors 25:4321.
meta.how_to_read: One row per room x today. Fill each step's {key} from the row's values, then the room's days.json card for the same today, then meta.constants. Dates read like "Mon 11 Nov", shares and % red as whole percents, money in euros (see harvest/explain.py display()).

best_day.title: Best harvest day
best_day.meaning: The day we estimate harvesting this room earns the most profit per m² for each day the crop has grown.
steps: Estimate how red the fruit is each day for the next 21 days, using {model_words}. Today: about {pct_red_now} red; future warmth is taken as {gdd_rate} a day, the average of the last 7 days.
For each day, estimate the share of pots ready to sell (a pot sells once one third of its fruit weight is red).

For each day, estimate profit: what the pots would sell for (fruit {fruit_weight_g} a pot, {density} pots per m²) minus all costs so far and the daily running cost of {cost_rate_m2_day}, divided by the days grown.

Pick the most profitable day among days with at least 95% of pots ready to sell: {best_day}. If the crop ripens a little faster or slower, the best day falls between {best_day_low} and {best_day_high}.
Days within 10% of the best day's profit make the optimal harvest zone: {optimal_from} to {optimal_to}.

caveats: Profit on days other than the actual harvest is a model estimate; each room was harvested once.
A cold or warm spell ahead moves the best day by a day or two.
Fruit dry matter (part of the real price) is not measured, so the lower price line is used.

pots_ready.title: Pots ready to sell today
pots_ready.meaning: The share of pots that would sell if the room were harvested today; a pot sells once one third of its fruit weight is red.
steps: Estimate how red the room is today: about {pct_red_now} of fruit weight (likely range {pct_red_low} to {pct_red_high}).
Pots ripen at different speeds, so spread the pots around that figure: plants differ by about {spread_sd} points of % red mid-ripening.
Count the pots at or above one third red: {sellable_share_now} of pots.

profit_best.title: Profit on the best day
profit_best.meaning: Estimated net profit per m² for each day grown, if the room is harvested on its best day.
steps: Sales: {density} pots per m² at about {price_per_pot} a pot (red fruit grams on the challenge price chart, unsellable pots earn nothing) = {revenue_m2}.
Costs up to the best day: plants, energy, fixed costs and re-spacing = {cost_to_date_m2}.
Net profit {net_m2} divided by {days_grown} days grown = {profit_best_m2_day}.
For comparison, harvesting today gives {profit_today_m2_day}.

confidence.title: How sure we are
confidence.meaning: How much to trust the best day, from three checks; the overall level is the weakest of the three.
steps: Day range: the likely range of the best day is {conf_day_range_days} wide ({conf_day_range_level}).
Agreement: do the warmth model, the camera and the latest crop sample agree on ripeness today? {conf_agreement} ({conf_agreement_level}).
Freshness: the older of the newest crop sample and the newest usable photo is {conf_freshness_days} old ({conf_freshness_level}).
Overall: {confidence}, the weakest of the three. Why: {conf_reasons}.

inputs.name: Agreement

caveats: Six rooms and one season: the day range is learned from only five other rooms.
Lamp-lit photos are not used for colour, so a room under lamps at noon can look stale.

look_day.title: Best shelf look
look_day.meaning: The first day the room is estimated to reach 70% red, where pots start to look their best (70–90% red).
steps: Start from today's estimate: about {pct_red_now} of fruit weight red.
Move forward day by day at {gdd_rate} of warmth a day on the room's ripening curve.
The first day at or above 70% red: {look_day}.

ship_day.title: Best day to pluck for Munich
ship_day.meaning: The day to pluck pots for Munich so no fruit weight is lost, the pots sell on arrival, and they stay in best condition on the shelf as long as possible.
steps: Fruit stops gaining weight on {weight_complete_day} (98% of final weight, curve fitted on the other rooms' weighings).
Munich is about 850 km away: {transit_days} on the road in a 13 °C truck, where pots keep ripening slowly.
Pots must arrive with at least 95% ready to sell, judged by the buyer on delivery.
Pluck day = the latest of those and today: {pluck_day}, because {pluck_reason_words}. Ship no later than {ship_by_day} to leave at least {min_shelf} in best condition.
